authoredPrompt: This figure contains four sub-panels (a through d) showing the different matrix representations used to encode a graph for graph neural networks. Panel a) depicts a 6-node undirected graph with nodes labeled 1 through 6, connected by edges whose identities are marked by the pair of endpoint node labels (e.g., ‘1\3’, ‘1\4’, ‘2\3’, ‘3\4’, ‘3\6’, ‘4\5’, ‘5\6’). Panel b) shows the adjacency matrix A (N × N), a square binary matrix encoding which pairs of nodes are connected by edges. Panel c) shows the node feature matrix X (D × N), in which each column stores the D-dimensional feature vector associated with one of the N nodes. Panel d) shows the edge feature matrix E (Dᴷ × E), in which each column stores the Dᴷ-dimensional feature vector associated with one of the E edges, with edges ordered to match the labeled pairs in panel a). Labels for each matrix include its name, symbol, and dimensions. This figure introduces the three standard data structures—adjacency matrix, node feature matrix, and edge feature matrix—that together fully represent a graph with node and edge attributes in a deep learning context.
authoredInteractions:
- Click a node (1–6) in the graph diagram to highlight its row and column in the adjacency matrix A and its column in the node data matrix X
- Click an edge between two nodes to highlight the corresponding entry in the edge data matrix E and the two nodes it connects
- Toggle between panels a–d to compare the visual graph, the N×N adjacency matrix, the D×N node data, and the D_E×E edge data representations

discrepancies: Panel a) is missing the signature per-node vertical feature bars (stacks of brown/orange squares) and per-edge feature bars (stacks of teal squares) that the source draws attached to every node and edge; the generated graph shows only bare circles and lines
Because the on-graph feature bars are absent, the visual link between a node/edge in panel a) and its column in matrices X and E is not visible at a glance, weakening the figure's core teaching point
Node/edge feature colors on the graph cannot be cross-checked against the matrices since the bars are not drawn, so the color-consistency story of the source is only half told
Matrix cell labels and panel titles render quite small at inline size compared to the source's larger, clearly readable annotations
evaluation.notes: The four-panel layout, graph topology (6 nodes / 7 edges), adjacency pattern, and the D×N and D_E×E feature matrices are all structurally correct, and the click-to-highlight cross-linking plus panel toggles and demo steps are genuinely pedagogical; however the generated panel a) omits the source's defining colored feature bars on every node and edge, so the graph no longer visually carries the feature vectors the figure is meant to illustrate.
action_items: In panel a), draw a vertical stack of 5 small colored squares (using nodeColors[id-1]) next to each node circle and a vertical stack of 4 teal squares (using edgeColors[][i]) near each edge midpoint, exactly as the source does, so each node/edge visibly carries its feature vector.

Make the on-graph node bar colors identical to the corresponding column of matrix X and the edge bar colors identical to the corresponding column of matrix E, so the highlight interaction shows a consistent color mapping.

Increase the font size of matrix row/column labels and the panel titles (Adjacency matrix A, Node data X, Edge data E) so they are comfortably legible at inline width, matching the source's larger annotations.
